description: Calculate one person’s daily hand-arm vibration (HAVS) exposure from the tools they use and for how long: A(8), HSE points, low/high range, and whether it passes the action value (2.5 m/s² A(8), 100 points) or the limit value (5 m/s², 400 points). For each tool give its own vibration figure in m/s², or an HSE category and variant to use HSE’s typical figure and range. Time means trigger time: the tool running in the person’s hands. Returns a link that opens the same calculation in the HAVS calculator.

tools.description: Tools or tasks used by one person during one day; 1 to 20 entries.

category.description: HSE tool category, used for HSE’s typical figure when vibration is omitted. Use other with a vibration value for anything else.

label.description: Optional task or tool label used in the result.

minutes.description: Actual exposure time in minutes, not the whole shift.

variant.description: HSE variant, needed when the category has several: drill (standard, hole-saw, core, impact); impact-wrench (small-drive, one-inch-drive); angle-grinder (small, flap-disc, large); sander (random-orbital, orbital); chipping-hammer (weld, stone); needle-scaler (standard, reduced); plate-compactor (standard, reduced); brushcutter (saw-head, strimmer-head).

vibration.description: Your own vibration value, m/s². The website rounds this input to two decimal places.

name: havs_daily_exposure

limit.description: What the result does not establish.

source.description: ComplyOnSite page that shows the same answer.

summary.description: The answer in one to three plain sentences, the figure or code first.

title: Calculate daily HAVS exposure
